subject: Context proration and seat bundling clarification
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@novaprod.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Question on billing behavior for long-context sessions + seats

Hi Connor,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Nova Product is excited about Redwood's latency profile. Before we move deeper in procurement, a couple practical pricing questions to confirm with my finance lead:

1) We plan to keep persistent long-context sessions (50k tokens) per user for our power-users. Do you bill that as full context per request, or is there any proration for reused KV/prefix caching across requests from the same session?

2) We anticipate a mixed consumption model: 20 named seats (editor users) + 500 occasional API-driven calls (background jobs). Can we bundle seats and API tokens in a single committed package, or are those strictly separate buckets?

3) Rounding / minimums: some of our background jobs generate tiny calls (a few tokens). Do you have a minimum per-request billing quantum or rounding policy we should model?

We need answers for a finance review Monday — any chance you can confirm or point me to a concise example?

Appreciate it,
Daniel
Director of Platform
Nova Product

P.S. cc'ing finance: finance@novaprod.com
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@novaprod.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 11:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Question on billing behavior for long-context sessions + seats

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then details and an example table attached.

1) Context reuse: We bill tokens emitted/consumed per request. If you use prefix/KV caching and the model does not re-stream the cached tokens, you are charged only for the new input + generated tokens. Persistent sessions that repeatedly resend the full 50k as part of the request will be billed for that transmitted context. We also support session-level KV caching for Private/Dedicated customers that avoids re-sending the unchanged prefix — that reduces token billing in practice.

2) Seats vs tokens: Committed packages are flexible — we can structure a single committed contract that covers named-seat entitlements (flat monthly fee) and a pooled token commitment for API usage. For budgeting we usually show seat fees separately and apply a blended unit price for committed token overage.

3) Minimum quantum: Our metering window uses a per-request quantum of 10 tokens for hosted API (we floor each request to nearest 10-token unit) to keep accounting practical; Dedicated can be configured with a 1-token quantum on contract. We can also white-glove suppliers for high-volume low-token workloads to apply a smoothing/aggregation rule so tiny calls don't blow up cost.

I've attached a short example (pricing-summary-v2.pdf) that lays out three scenarios with worked numbers. If helpful, we can map this to your estimated traffic and propose a committed package + a pilot concession for the first 3 months.

Want to schedule a 30-min call today to go through finance's specific numbers? Marissa (cc) leads our pricing for committed contracts and Ben (cc) can run the seat bundling examples.

—Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 13:00:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: Question on billing behavior for long-context sessions + seats

Marissa, Ben — forwarding Daniel's ask (Nova Product). Quick internal note:

Summary of negotiation levers I think will help close:
- Offer: 12-month committed token pool (2.5B tokens/month) + 20 named-seat license at $X/seat/month.
- Quantum adjustment: For pilot (first 90 days) reduce hosted quantum from 10-token floor to 1-token smoothing for their background jobs (approx 500 calls/day at ~6 tokens/call). After pilot revert to standard or transition to Dedicated where quantum = 1.
- Context caching: Recommend Private/Dedicated pilot to enable session KV cache which will materially cut token usage for the 50k long-context flows.
- Discount: propose a blended 18% discount on committed token unit price for the first year, with review at Q4.
- Credits: offer one month of token credit (equal to 10% of first three months' forecast) if we miss agreed latency SLO for >2 sustained incidents during pilot.

Risks and ask: Procurement will push to treat seats as included in the token pool (they want fungibility). Legal will push back; seats are normally priced separately. If we concede, we should: (a) cap fungible seat+token drawdown to avoid gaming, (b) add an overage price band so we preserve revenue.

Could you both review and advise on allowable concession range? My thought: up to 20% discount + pilot quantum adjustment is acceptable, but seat fungibility should be limited to 10% of token pool.

Connor

[Internal — do not share outside Redwood]
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@novaprod.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 08:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Question on billing behavior for long-context sessions + seats

Hi Daniel — following up with a concrete proposal for your finance review. I tried to keep the MAPlike items concise so procurement can route to legal.

Mutual Action Plan (high level):
- Week 0: Sign term sheet (DocuSign link below) for a 12-month committed package.
- Week 1–4: Kickoff + telemetry integration; we run an ingestion run to baseline token usage.
- Month 1–3 (pilot): Apply the temporary quantum smoothing for hosted API (counts floored to 1-token equivalent for background jobs). Provide one month of token credit equivalent to 10% of forecasted month-1 usage if we miss latency SLO > 2 incidents.
- Month 4+: Move billing to standard quantum (10-token floor) unless you opt for Dedicated/Private, in which case we switch to 1-token meter.

Commercials (summary — see attached pricing-summary-v2.pdf for line items):
- 12-month committed token pool: 2,500,000,000 tokens/month at $0.0000125/token (blended after 18% first-year discount).
- 20 named seats: $55/seat/month (seats billed separately).
- Seat fungibility: up to 10% of committed token pool may be consumed by seat-intensive workloads (we'll model expected drawdown during onboarding). Any usage beyond that will be charged at the committed overage unit price.

Governance & next steps:
- HubSpot deal created: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/75432/NB-2028-0719-01
- DocuSign term sheet: https://www.docusign.com/link/ABC123456789
- Please confirm by EOD Mon if the pilot concession on quantum and the 18% discount move forward so I can route to legal.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if you want to run numbers live.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Connor.obrien@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
